title: News: US inflation came in hot, Bitcoin dropped

linkedin.text:
Yesterday the US inflation number for September came in at 3.7% a year. Markets expected 3.6%.

A 0.1 percentage point miss sounds like nothing. Bitcoin fell about $1,000 within minutes, the 10-year US Treasury yield jumped to around 5.3%, and stock futures slipped.

Why such a big reaction to such a small gap? Because prices already reflected the forecast. What moves markets is the surprise.

Hotter inflation raises the odds that the US central bank lifts interest rates again. Higher rates make safe government bonds pay more, and some money leaves risky assets like crypto to chase that safer return.

Three takeaways if you hold crypto:

1. Know the big calendar dates. Inflation data and central bank meetings regularly move crypto more than crypto news does.
2. Expect swings around them and size your positions so a $1,000 move doesn't force a decision.
3. Don't panic-sell a red candle you could have seen coming.

Source: CoinDesk, 14 Oct 2026.

Education, not financial advice.
